transcript.text: Bosch HBS534BS0B oven displaying E011 and won't let me do anything. Beeping. Help!

The E011 code on Bosch ovens is ambiguous in general databases, but with your symptoms (beeping and locked controls), the most common cause is a control panel issue—specifically a button that is stuck down or shorted. This prevents the oven from accepting commands. Please press each button on the control panel individually to see if any feel stuck or don't click normally. If all buttons feel fine, it could be a fault with the temperature sensor (which stops cooking for safety) or the main control board. Let me know what you find with the buttons first.

Pressed them all, none feel stuck and they all click/respond normally as far as I can tell, but nothing happens. Should mention it started right after I wiped the panel with a wet cloth and kitchen spray.

Given that this started immediately after using a wet cloth and spray on the controls, it is almost certain that moisture has seeped behind the fascia and caused a short circuit in the control panel. This triggers the safety lockout (E011) and prevents operation. Please unplug the oven from the mains for at least 24 hours to allow any trapped moisture to evaporate completely. If the fault persists after this drying period, the liquid has likely caused permanent damage to the control electronics, and you will need an engineer to replace the faulty component.

It's built in so I switched it off at the cooker switch instead, after drying the panel with a towel. Left it 5 minutes, and it's come back up normally with no code. Is that okay, or do I still need the full 24 hours?

Since the oven has reset and is working normally after just 5 minutes, the moisture has evaporated quickly enough to clear the fault. You do not need to wait the full 24 hours. To prevent this from happening again, try to avoid spraying cleaning products directly onto the control panel; instead, spray them onto a cloth first and then wipe the buttons.

candidates: Control panel button stuck or shorted (high)

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
